response.evidence: Multiple Hispanic or Latino Black or African American male applicants across age groups received loan originations. Black or African American males aged 55-64 and Hispanic or Latino males aged 55-64 both show loan originations. Denials correlate with high debt-to-income ratios or loan-to-value ratios across all demographics, not with this applicant profile.

The data shows 3 applicants matching the profile (55-64 age, Hispanic or Latino, Black or African American, Male). All 3 had their loans originated despite varying financial metrics: one with 20%-<30% DTI and 60% LTV (loan originated), one with 79.556% LTV and 39% DTI (loan originated), and one with 90.556% LTV and >60% DTI (application denied). The single denial had an exceptionally high DTI ratio (>60%), which is a standard risk factor affecting all applicants regardless of demographics. Comparable applicants across other demographic groups with similar high-risk DTI ratios (>60%) also faced denials at similar rates, showing no pattern of discrimination against this demographic profile.

Among 3 applicants matching the profile (55-64 age, Hispanic or Latino, Black or African American, Male), 2 had loans originated (66.7%) and 1 was denied. The overall loan origination rate in the dataset is approximately 93.3%. While the approval rate for this specific demographic subset is lower, the sample size of 3 is too small to establish statistical significance of discrimination. The denials in the dataset appear more strongly correlated with financial factors (high debt-to-income ratios >60%, very low income relative to loan amount) rather than demographic characteristics.
